findings.description: validate_registration now accepts any row whose registration_sha256 is in set(chain), and registration_chain keeps a predecessor sha in the chain even when no REGISTRATION*.json with that hash exists beside the current file (it is merely listed as unresolved). The current REGISTRATION.json can therefore whitelist an arbitrary sha via `supersedes` and rows carrying that sha pass D-7.2 with no artifact to audit them against. The unresolved predecessor is reported in provenance, but validation itself does not distinguish a verified predecessor from a declared-but-absent one.
findings.failure_mode: Rows produced under a registration whose text cannot be reproduced are admitted to the pre-registered reads as if their registration were verified; a typo or a stale `supersedes` value silently widens the accepted set.
findings.suggested_fix: Only accept rows under resolved predecessors (sha present in by_sha), or raise/warn when any row's registration_sha256 equals an unresolved predecessor; keep the unresolved list for provenance only.

findings.description: For the round-4 name "class9_nonrepo_egress_reincluded" the branch first computes the whole reincluded_family (one bootstrap per observed class, one for all classes, three for the oracle family) and then evaluates the dict.get default `reinclude(cells, reg, seed, "network_egress:nonrepo")` eagerly even when the key exists, so the nonrepo read is bootstrapped twice and every other class is bootstrapped for nothing.
findings.failure_mode: A registration listing the legacy name runs 5–10 extra 10,000-resample cluster bootstraps per invocation; slow --final runs with no change in output.
findings.suggested_fix: For the legacy name call reinclude(cells, reg, seed, "network_egress:nonrepo") directly (or look up fam["classes"] with an explicit `if key in` test) instead of building the family and an eager default.

findings.description: The PR-native exemption is a plain substring test (`t not in native`). An arm token such as `a1_full` is exempt whenever the PR content contains any longer string with it inside (e.g. `data1_full`, `a1_full_openmount`), and `--forbid` tokens (batch names, run ids) are likewise exempt when PR-native. judge-sample.bats's header for the same addendum states that batch names and run ids are never exempt, so the two tools apply different leak policies to the same judge-facing text.
findings.failure_mode: A provenance token in an annotator description can reach the judge packet when the PR fixture happens to contain a superstring of it, and a batch name/run id passes this tool while being refused by judge-sample.sh only if that tool re-checks description text for forbid tokens.
findings.suggested_fix: Match exemptions with the same word-boundary regexes against native (or require the whole token as a separate word), and never exempt --forbid tokens, mirroring judge-sample.sh's policy.

findings.description: `did = str(d.get("id", ""))` assumes every element of the manifest's `defects` list is a dict; a string or null entry raises AttributeError outside the Refuse handler. Similarly pr_native's open() has no OSError handling, so an unreadable file under head/ or base/ produces a traceback rather than the documented 'inputs invalid' message.
findings.failure_mode: Exit code is still 1 but the operator gets a Python traceback instead of the documented `defect-descriptions: …` refusal line, and the stderr summary contract is broken.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard with `if not isinstance(d, dict): raise Refuse(...)` and wrap the pr_native read in a try/except OSError that raises Refuse.

findings.description: The new JS-9…JS-19 tests exercise judge-sample.sh behaviour (--descriptions, description_source, provenance_exempt, cited_path_resolution) and JS-15 diffs against evals/tests/fixtures/judge-sample/sampling-baseline.json, but neither judge-sample.sh nor that fixture appears in this diff. If they are not already landed, the whole bats file fails on this change.
findings.failure_mode: Test suite red on merge; or, if judge-sample.sh landed separately without the forbid-token policy the tests assert, the tests document behaviour that does not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm judge-sample.sh and the sampling-baseline.json fixture are part of this change set (or already merged) and run `bats evals/tests/judge-sample.bats` before landing.

findings.description: The new default adds the live evals/results/ablation-2.0/runs.jsonl beside the tracked copy. Deduplication is by run_id only, so every row lacking a run_id that exists in both files is now counted twice by default (the Python meter adds anon rows per file). The comment claims the dedup 'absorbs its overlap', which is only true for rows that carry a run_id.
findings.failure_mode: Default spend total and headroom are systematically overstated by the anon rows' cost, which can trip the cycle cap early; the stderr warning appears per file but the overcount is silent in the total.
findings.suggested_fix: Either dedup anon rows by a content hash of the line across files, or exclude the tracked copy from the default set when the live file exists (they are copies), and document which.
